subject: Medix: performance debrief, recommended models & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Levine <jenna@medix.ai>, Tom Carter <tom.carter@medix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Medix: performance debrief, recommended models & next steps

Hi Jenna / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and concrete next steps so we can line up the evals you asked for.

Recap (what we discussed)
- Primary production goal: high-quality clinical note summarization + extraction for downstream billing (low to medium prompt complexity).
- SLO targets: 95th pct latency < 120 ms for short requests (<= 512 tokens), 99th pct < 300 ms for worst-case interactive flows.
- Expected peak TPS: 55–80 concurrent inference requests during daytime windows.

Redwood recommendations (initial candidates)
1) redwood/titan-l-16q (recommended baseline) — high quality, good cost/perf; verified throughput ~70 TPS on a 4xA100 pool; 95th pct latency 98 ms; 99th pct latency 240 ms (see attached profile).
2) open-run/neo-4x-quant (low-cost fallback) — slightly lower quality on abstractive summarization but excellent peak TPS; verified ~120 TPS when sharded; 95th pct 110 ms at medium batch sizes.
3) redwood/clarion-english-2 (higher-quality option) — best QA/extraction fidelity with 95th pct ~140 ms; heavier cost.

Key concerns raised (quality regression risks)
- Prompt sensitivity on rare medical abbreviations; we flagged a small prompt-set mismatch and recommend adding 75 canonical examples from your historical logs (we attached medix_prompt_set_v1.txt).
- Tokenization edge cases for certain ICD phrases — we'll add a targeted eval for those in the test harness.

Attachments shared
- redwood_perf_profiles_medix_q1.pdf (Redwood-verified perf profiles with TPS/latency percentiles and cost estimates)
- medix_prompt_set_v1.txt (seed prompt set you can review/edit)
- bench-run-setup-instructions.md (how we run the Redwood bench harness in your environment)

Immediate next steps (please confirm):
1) You confirm which candidate(s) to run full evaluator against (pick up to 2): baseline + one high-quality or low-cost fallback.
2) Grant access to one sample dataset (S3 link or drive) and a short list of the top 10 intents to prioritize for the first run.
3) Schedule a 45m follow-up on Monday to review initial bench results (I suggested a calendar link below).

Links
- Perf profiles: https://drive.redwood.ai/medix/perf-profiles/redwood_perf_profiles_medix_q1.pdf
- Initial bench run placeholder: https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/medix-initial-202701
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-2027-0041

Thanks — I attached the perf PDF and the prompt set. If you want, we can start with titan-l-16q + neo-4x-quant and run the first 2k-sample pass this week.

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the run: 

1) For the titan-l-16q baseline, can you confirm the 99th percentile latency numbers at a sustained 70 TPS with a 512-token cap? We need to make sure our UI remains snappy for clinicians.
2) For the neo-4x-quant fallback, what's the expected drop in extraction F1 (roughly)? If we're trading quality for cost we want to contain the false negative rate for key billing entities.

We'll aim to share a sanitized S3 bucket with 2k example docs by tomorrow EOD. Also including our Sr. Platform engineer (Tom) to coordinate the access pattern.

Subject: Re: Medix: performance debrief, recommended models & next steps

Jenna — quick internal note to clarify the 99th pct question and rollout path.

- Verified numbers: titan-l-16q @ sustained 70 TPS, 512 tokens -> 99th pct ~ 255–265 ms on our 4xA100 config when KV cache warming is considered. We saw spikes up to ~300 ms for certain long-context warmups; that's why we included the cache warmup guidance in bench-run-setup-instructions.md.
- Canary suggestion: start with 5% traffic on titan-l-16q and autoscale up to 25% while monitoring 99th pct and F1 on extraction tasks. If 99th pct passes and extraction F1 (on the seeded prompt set) stays within -1.5% of baseline, ramp to 60–75%.
- Fallback: auto-route to neo-4x-quant when GPU queue depth exceeds threshold OR when latency breaches soft-SLO for 3 consecutive minutes. This keeps UI availability while limiting cost.

I also added a quick cost delta estimate in the attached perf PDF — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions – Redwood Inference
